strengths: Clear motivation addressing genuine limitations in text-to-3D generation with a principled VLM-based solution
Comprehensive quantitative validation on GPTEval3D benchmark with consistent improvements over all baselines (DreamReward, DreamDPO, etc.) across all 6 metrics
Demonstrated generality across two distinct paradigms (optimization-based SDS and feed-forward models) without requiring retraining
Well-designed ablation studies validating the necessity of geometric query and multi-view inputs
Compelling qualitative results showing recovery of semantic content and correction of spatial inconsistencies
Sound technical approach with end-to-end differentiable pipeline and clever dual-query design
Practical applicability with reasonable computational overhead
Honest discussion of limitations and concrete suggestions for future directions
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for why log-odds formulation is optimal; no comparison with alternative VLM-based reward designs
Only one VLM backbone tested (Qwen2.5-VL 7B); generality across different VLM architectures unvalidated
Missing critical implementation details for reproducibility: learning rates, optimizer settings, formally specified annealing schedule for λ_VLM
No human evaluation; reliance on automated metrics potentially biases results toward VLM preferences and artifacts
Limited failure mode analysis; only one detailed example of acknowledged limitations with very long prompts
Incomplete analysis of test-time guidance application: computational cost breakdown unclear, limited baseline comparisons for feed-forward paradigm
Potential VLM biases and hallucinations not discussed; no analysis of conflicting semantic/geometric objectives
No code release mentioned; exact prompt templates and rendering parameters not fully specified in main text, hindering reproduction
